reason: The array's buckled feet need support, and the available steel could provide it.
expectation: The steel will repair or replace the array's damaged feet.

effect: The array now stands on steel feet, ready for its loose lead to be connected.
reaction: The broad feet and cable slack make the repair feel physically sensible.
reason: The loose external lead needs reconnecting, and the power cable is the obvious match for the standing array.
expectation: The cable will connect the array to the power system.

effect: The solar array is online and supplying the station, so I can address the reserve connection.
reaction: The isolated controller makes reconnecting the lead feel sensible.
reason: The reserve charging connection is the obvious destination for the restored solar supply.
expectation: The solar supply will connect to and begin charging the reserve.

effect: The reserve is charging, and replenishing breathing oxygen is now the goal.
reaction: The distinction between essential loads and industrial work makes the reserve's limits clear.
reason: The atmospheric processor seems relevant to oxygen replenishment, but its required partner isn't clear.
expectation: Its available partners should show how to begin producing oxygen.

effect: The processor is running on solar power and replenishing oxygen; the remaining goal is to hear from Earth.
reaction: The explanation of splitting atmospheric carbon dioxide was useful.
reason: The bent antenna likely needs straightening before it can be mounted for the radio.
expectation: The service tool will repair the antenna for mounting.

effect: The antenna is upright and can be aimed, so it appears ready for the radio mount.
reaction: Straightening the stay and refastening its hinge was a clear repair.
reason: Mounting the straightened antenna should help restore contact with Earth.
expectation: The antenna will be connected to the radio so it can receive a signal.

effect: Mounting the antenna restored radio contact and completed the chapter; the message from Earth was recorded.
reaction: The recorded message made the first contact feel personal without implying an immediate conversation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Starting the atmospheric processor was most worthwhile: it connected the power repair to a useful explanation of extracting oxygen from carbon dioxide.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the standing array to the cable was straightforward progress, but less interesting than the repairs and discoveries around it.

surprise.text: I learned that the reserve could sustain essential systems through an interruption but not industrial work.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the repairs and connections had clear purposes.

continue.text: Yes. The physically grounded repairs and oxygen-production explanation were engaging, and the recorded message leaves me curious about the expedition.
